summary: The proposal presents a coherent, technically concrete problem, four action-form objectives, suitable UML diagrams, a detailed bibliography, an adequate AI transparency statement, and an agile-looking schedule with measurable outcomes. The main issues are that the Problem section includes a workaround/solution discussion despite the requirement to describe only problems, and the substantive proposal appears longer than the 4–6-page limit once the required non-schedule text is counted. Tighten the Problem section and reduce the proposal text while preserving the objective structure and evidence.

findings.title: Remove the workaround from the Problem section
findings.description: The Problem section introduces a workaround/solution rather than limiting itself to the problem and its consequences. Recast this as a description of the underlying risk (maintainers lacking appropriate decision capability and administrators becoming a bottleneck), without presenting the workaround as an alternative or proposed remedy.

locations.quote: The common workaround hands maintainers full administrative rights, which violates the principle of least privilege [SS75] and exposes every user and every host to a mistake made for a single project.

findings.title: Reduce the proposal text to the allowed length
findings.description: The proposal is substantially longer than the permitted 4–6 pages of proposal text: the substantive sections span pages 2–9, before the bibliography and transparency statement. Condense the proposal text to at most six pages, or remove nonessential detail while retaining the required sections and objective descriptions.

locations.quote: The thesis runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. I divide the work into six iterations of four weeks, each ending with a vertically integrated increment
